summary: Instagram is doing most of the work: nearly every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 50 views. The best videos show a robot or a simple gadget behaving in a surprising way, with a short hook about what it can't do (no gyro, no clapping, no brain). Plain 'How does X work?' videos on public gadgets (taps, doors, smoke alarms, street lights) get far less reach and almost no saves or shares.
winningPattern: Hindi videos about robots or hobby-style modules (gyro, clap switch, PIR, line follower, mic) with a 'surprise negation' title: 'X doesn't do the obvious thing, it only does Y' or 'Without X, this fails instantly'. Short, punchy Hinglish title with one emoji. Posted on Instagram Reels first, where saves and shares come from the maker-style demo. Published Oct 29 to Nov 2 and the newest ones are climbing.
doMore: Lead with a robot or Arduino module doing something surprising, and show the failure or odd behaviour in the first second
Use the 'Nahi... sirf...' title format (e.g. Clap Switch Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai)
Make the video worth saving: show one pin, wiring or part name on screen so makers bookmark it
Post to Instagram first and treat YouTube as a secondary test, repurposing only the top performers
Keep the cadence of the last week, since recent videos beat the October batch
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' videos on everyday public gadgets (tap, mall door, lift, street light)
Near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos, two IR sensor videos, two automatic tap videos) that split the audience
Posting English-only or YouTube-only videos, since the English Arduino video got no Instagram reach
